title: AWS deployment: architecture
summary: How Personalisation Hub is built: its microservice components, the AWS services it runs on, and why it uses Kubernetes on EKS.
bodyMd:
Personalisation Hub runs as a set of microservices on Amazon EKS inside your own AWS account, with managed AWS services for data, messaging, search and encryption. This page describes the parts and why the platform is built this way.

The Installation Wizard

The CloudFormation template you launch from AWS Marketplace creates a small EC2 instance that hosts the Installation Wizard. The wizard is a one-step deployer: once you have created the Master Admin account and chosen the environment type, size and platform domain, it provisions the complete platform stack into your AWS account using Terraform. The same wizard later serves the Cost Control settings page.

Platform components

The platform is modular and distributed, so each component can scale independently.

ComponentWhat it does
Auth APIUser authentication, roles and permissions
Campaign Mobile and Campaign APIAccess to the campaign repository, with localisation and personalisation by store, display and visitor
Retail AdminStore staff view and update retail data, control localised campaign playback, and manage queues and appointments
HQ AdminHead-office management of localised and personalised campaigns across all stores, displays and devices, including hardware, software/CMS, third-party integrations and visitor identification
Store QueuingLets customers join a queue and surfaces integrated customer data to retail staff
JCRIntegration layer to Adobe Experience Manager through Java Content Repository APIs
Location APILocalised data for refining campaign targeting; hosts the Visitor API for customer data matching
MISTProximity-based targeting inside the store
Background TaskDaemon service for background jobs and scheduling
Monitoring ToolsPrometheus and Grafana for issue detection and performance monitoring
Location ToolkitReceives campaign playback data from displays; provides performance reporting and issue alerts
Squid proxyOutbound communication with external parties
Adobe Experience ManagerAEM content and interactions, where AEM is in use

AWS services used

ServiceRole in the platform
Amazon EKSRuns the Kubernetes clusters that host the components
Amazon RDSPostgreSQL databases
Amazon S3Platform data and assets
AWS KMSEncryption keys for data at rest
Amazon ElastiCache for RedisCaching for platform performance
Amazon MSKKafka for high-volume, real-time data streams
Amazon SNSEmail and SMS messaging
Amazon OpenSearch ServiceScalable search for logging and monitoring

Why Kubernetes on EKS

Running the platform on a managed Kubernetes service shapes most of its operational characteristics:

  • Less cluster management. EKS abstracts the Kubernetes control plane, so operation focuses on the application rather than the cluster.
  • Scaling and availability. Worker nodes and pods scale automatically with demand, which also keeps cost in line with usage.
  • Native AWS integration. The cluster works directly with EC2, Elastic Load Balancing, RDS, S3 and the other services in the table.
  • Security and compliance. IAM integration, network isolation in a VPC, encryption, audit logging and CloudTrail integration come from the AWS platform itself.
  • Portability. Standard Kubernetes APIs mean workloads can move between environments.
  • Automated deployment. Containerised components support CI/CD-style automated deployment.
